Functions Detection

Source: R/intern_.functions_detect.R
dot-functions_detect.Rd

Detect the names of the functions called in the code of a function.

Usage

.functions_detect(x, skipped_base, arg_user_setting2, lib_path, error_text)

Arguments

x

Function to analyze.

skipped_base

Vector of strings: names not reported (e.g., "function" or "if").

arg_user_setting2

List of the arguments written in the call of the calling function (arg_user_setting of the calling function). Its x compartment, the name of the analyzed function, is used in the messages and for the recursive calls (see fun_names_internal below).

lib_path

Vector of character strings or NULL: the lib_path value of the calling exported function, only passed on to arg_check() (directly or through the internal functions called). No default value.

error_text

Single character string added to the error messages to name the calling functions (embed_error_text of the calling function). NULL is converted into "". No default value.

Value

A list:

  • code: vector of strings, the lines of the printed code of x, with the runs of spaces collapsed into one space, and the leading space and the comments removed.

  • all_basic_funs: vector of strings, names of all the objects of the basic R environments of the search path (packages stats, graphics, grDevices, utils, datasets, methods and base, and Autoloads), which must all be attached, otherwise an error is returned.

  • fun_names: list of vectors of strings, the names followed by ( in each line of code, and the names of called functions ending a line, their ( being on a next line (names given as calls by the parse data or, if the printed code does not parse, any name ending a line followed by a line starting with (), except the names of skipped_base. Only lines with names are present, the compartment names indicating the line numbers (e.g., "c3" for line 3).

  • fun_names_pos: list as fun_names, with the position of the first character of each name in its line.

  • code_line_nb: vector of integers, the line numbers of the compartments of fun_names.

  • arg_user_setting: arg_user_setting2, with x written "pkg::fun()" if x is written pkg::fun in the call.

  • fun_names_skip: list as fun_names, with TRUE for the names not to check: names inside a formula or inside the arguments of a call of quote(), bquote(), expression(), alist() or substitute() (written without package or after base:: or base:::, possibly between quotes, also with the value piped into it), except the code that R evaluates (arguments of the .() and, if splice is TRUE or T, ..() calls of bquote(), where of bquote() and env of substitute(), none if R cannot match their arguments), and name of the function called by .Internal() (e.g., toupper in .Internal(toupper(x))).

  • fun_names_internal: list as fun_names, with TRUE for the calls of internal functions inside their scope: formal arguments of x and name of x (x compartment of arg_user_setting2, possibly written pkg::name or followed by (), if the function of this name found from the environment of x is x: recursive calls) in the whole code of x, formal arguments of a function defined in x inside this definition (not for a definition in quoted code, see fun_names_skip), and names assigned a function definition or a utils::getFromNamespace() result (<-, =, ->) inside the innermost function definition containing the assignment (the innermost one outside the quoted code if the assignment is not quoted, none if this definition is in quoted code, and the whole code of x for <<-, ->>).

NULL, with a warning, if x is a primitive function (no R code), or if the code of x has no name followed by ( other than the names of skipped_base.

Details

The names between quotes (e.g., "paste(x)") are reported. The comments are removed beforehand, the quotes being read as the R parser does (see .in_quotes_replacement()).

The existence of the reported functions is not checked.

The internal functions, the formulas, the calls of quote(), bquote(), expression(), alist() and substitute(), and the .Internal() calls are found in the parse data of the printed code of x. If this code does not parse (e.g., an environment object inserted in the body of x), the formulas, these quoting calls and the .Internal() calls are not detected, and the internal functions are only the name of x and the names written name <- function( or name <- utils::getFromNamespace( at the beginning of a line, in the whole code of x.

Warnings:

  • Requires saferDev::arg_check, .extract_all_fun_names, .in_quotes_replacement.

  • In the safer Backbone section "######## check of the required functions from the required packages", add also these 3 functions when checking for the presence of .functions_detect.
